title: DiagramCloud capabilities (self-description)
summary: What DiagramCloud does, how it is used (browser studio, CLI commands, stdio MCP tools, import and export formats), how it is built, where it comes from and where it stops. Every statement cites a file and line of the public repository at the recorded source cut. Static source only: nothing here was observed running, reviewed or certified; runtime and verification stay UNKNOWN unless a cited line says otherwise.
provenance: Explicit source-bound authoring brief. No code, tool, scan or provider is executed. No observation or approval is created.

blocks.title: Selected capability scope
blocks.text:
Author a project as one validated document
Surfaces: Browser studio, JSON file
Version: 1.29.1 at source cut ecf4af6
Environment: Local browser (Chromium is the qualified browser)
Captured: 2026-10-19T00:00:00Z
Declarations below may coexist. A frozen lifecycle does not remove a previously delivered feature.

blocks.title: How to use
blocks.text: Open the studio (npm ci, then npm run dev with Node.js 22). Explore is read-only; Edit adds components, connections, child views, evidence, sources and undo; Portfolio shows the public projection.

blocks.title: How it is built
blocks.text: Every document goes through validateDocument in src/core/model.ts. Evidence blocks carry a provenance from a fixed vocabulary (source-derived, synthetic, reference, author).

blocks.title: Limits and alternatives
blocks.text: DiagramCloud is not a cloud runtime, IDE, notebook kernel, query engine, Git or task authority. Code and rows are displayed, never executed. Chromium is the only qualified browser.

blocks.title: Selected capability scope
blocks.text:
Share only the public projection
Surfaces: Browser studio, Exports
Version: 1.29.1 at source cut ecf4af6
Environment: Local browser and CLI
Captured: 2026-10-19T00:00:00Z
Declarations below may coexist. A frozen lifecycle does not remove a previously delivered feature.

blocks.title: How it is built
blocks.text: publicDocument in src/core/operations.ts builds the public copy that every export reads.

blocks.title: Checks and trust boundaries
blocks.text: Credential-like values are refused where content crosses an app boundary, but this is not secret scanning, DLP or access control: a sensitive fact marked public stays public.

blocks.title: Selected capability scope
blocks.text:

Surfaces: Browser studio, JSON patch

Environment: Local browser
Captured: 2026-10-19T00:00:00Z
Declarations below may coexist. A frozen lifecycle does not remove a previously delivered feature.

blocks.title: How to use
blocks.text: An observation arrives as a patch through the JSON / AI review; it arrives private, unreviewed and not shareable, and only a person reviews it in Edit mode.

blocks.title: Limits and alternatives
blocks.text: Observations are one-time reviewed imports, not subscriptions; DiagramCloud never polls another app. A scan is never observed.

Diagram a repository from its declarations
Surfaces: Browser studio, CLI
Version: 1.29.1 at source cut ecf4af6
Environment: Local browser or Node.js 22 command line
Captured: 2026-10-19T00:00:00Z
Declarations below may coexist. A frozen lifecycle does not remove a previously delivered feature.

blocks.title: How to use
blocks.text: CLI: npm run scan -- <folder> --out repo.json. In the browser: Diagram from a repository in the gallery.

blocks.title: How it is built
blocks.text: scanRepository in src/core/scan/scanner.ts is the deterministic scanner shared by the browser and the CLI.

blocks.title: Limits and alternatives
blocks.text: It reads declarations, not runtime behaviour: no call graph, no traffic, imports only for TypeScript/JavaScript and Python, Terraform by pattern.

blocks.text:
Join several repositories in one atlas
Surfaces: CLI, Browser studio
Version: 1.29.1 at source cut ecf4af6
Environment: Node.js 22 command line
Captured: 2026-10-19T00:00:00Z
Declarations below may coexist. A frozen lifecycle does not remove a previously delivered feature.

blocks.title: How to use
blocks.text: Write a project manifest, then npm run atlas -- project.manifest.json --out atlas.json; add --previous to compare revision vectors.

blocks.title: Limits and alternatives
blocks.text: Membership comes only from the manifest; repositories are read like a scan, read-only, without git commands or network.

Surfaces: Browser studio

Captured: 2026-10-19T00:00:00Z
Declarations below may coexist. A frozen lifecycle does not remove a previously delivered feature.

blocks.title: How to use
blocks.text: Choose Import draw.io / Mermaid / Visio in the gallery. Accepted files include .drawio, .xml, .drawio.svg, .drawio.png, .mmd, .mermaid, .md and Visio .vsdx.

blocks.title: Limits and alternatives
blocks.text: Adapters with a loss report: no styles or vendor artwork, no binary .vsd, no lossless Mermaid round trip.

blocks.title: How to use
blocks.text: Use the export menu of the studio. Interactive HTML, SVG, Mermaid, draw.io, PowerPoint and the technical manual each read the public projection.

blocks.title: Limits and alternatives
blocks.text: PPTX is a semantic reconstruction, not a pixel copy of arbitrary layouts.

blocks.text:
Draw publication figures
Surfaces: CLI, Browser studio
Version: 1.29.1 at source cut ecf4af6
Environment: Node.js 22 command line or local browser
Captured: 2026-10-19T00:00:00Z
Declarations below may coexist. A frozen lifecycle does not remove a previously delivered feature.

blocks.title: How to use
blocks.text: npm run design -- doc.json --out figures/ writes one SVG per view, an index, a figure book and suggestions; --brief applies a design brief in memory.

blocks.title: How it is built
blocks.text: recommendFigures in src/export/design/recommend.ts ranks figure suggestions.

blocks.title: Origins and reuse
blocks.text: The visual grammar is adapted from diagram-design (MIT, attributed); no code, icons or fonts are copied.

Environment: Node.js 22 command line
Captured: 2026-10-19T00:00:00Z

blocks.title: How to use
blocks.text: npm run intelligence -- <mode> --input <file> --out <new-directory>. Modes include inspect, brief, graph, query, catalogue, suggest-mapping and validate-proposal.

blocks.title: Checks and trust boundaries
blocks.text: No network, no execution of analysed code, no remote upload; the output directory must be new and existing files are never overwritten.

blocks.title: How to use
blocks.text: npm run intelligence:mcp -- <selected-document.json>. Tools include diagramcloud_query, diagramcloud_render, diagramcloud_catalogue and diagramcloud_validate_proposal.

blocks.title: Limits and alternatives
blocks.text: No listener, arbitrary paths, mutations, execution, polling, settings changes or model.

blocks.title: Limits and alternatives

blocks.text: Original source is MIT licensed; dependencies keep their own terms.

blocks.text: Named UI component library under its upstream MIT licence. Version UNKNOWN in this guide.

blocks.title: React Flow (@xyflow/react)
blocks.text: Draws the interactive canvas; the domain model stays independent of it. MIT licence. Version UNKNOWN in this guide.

blocks.title: Zod
blocks.text: Schema library used by the document validator. MIT licence. Version UNKNOWN in this guide.

blocks.title: PptxGenJS
blocks.text: Builds the PowerPoint export. MIT licence. Version UNKNOWN in this guide.

blocks.title: web-tree-sitter
blocks.text: Optional syntax runtime with pinned local grammars; analysed code is never executed and no grammar is fetched.

blocks.title: Browser IndexedDB
blocks.text: Projects are stored in the browser; there is no server, account or database.

blocks.title: diagram-design visual grammar
blocks.text: Diagram Design mode adapts the visual grammar of diagram-design (MIT, attributed). DiagramCloud renderers are an independent implementation; no code, icons or fonts are copied.
